claim: Cliff-destruction status bit WBCL1R = $20 disables/destroys CLIFF1R — a WSTATUS high-nibble bit jt3-2 makes behaviour (JOUSTRV4.SRC:190).

source.verbatim: WBCL1R	EQU	$20	IF=1, CLIFF1R IS DISABLED (OR DESTROYED)

claim: Cliff-destruction status bit WBCL2 = $40 disables/destroys CLIFF2 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:191).

source.verbatim: WBCL2	EQU	$40	IF=1, CLIFF2 IS DISABLED (OR DESTROYED)

claim: Cliff-destruction status bit WBCL4 = $80 disables/destroys CLIFF4 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:192).

source.verbatim: WBCL4	EQU	$80	IF=1, CLIFF4 IS DISABLED (OR DESTROYED)

claim: WCLFTB row for CLIF1L: FCB WBCL1L($10),$01,$03 — status bit, LNDXTB landing bit cleared, BCKXTB collision bits cleared (both CLIF1L $01 and CLIF1R $02) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2407).
WCLFTB row for CLIF1R: FCB WBCL1R($20),$00,$00 — landing/background bytes are $00 because CLIF1R shares CLIF1L's merged ledge bit $01 and its side is cleared by CLIF1L's $03 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2409).
WCLFTB row for CLIF2: FCB WBCL2($40),$02,$04 — landing bit $02 (LNDB1) and background bit $04 cleared on destroy (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2411).
WCLFTB row for CLIF4: FCB WBCL4($80),$10,$40 — landing bit $10 (LNDB4) and background bit $40 cleared on destroy (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2413).
WCLFEW destroy path clears the cliff's landing bit (byte 1 of the WCLFTB record) from the RAM landing table LNDXD1 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2310).
WCLFEW destroy path clears the cliff's background-collision bit (byte 2 of the WCLFTB record) from the RAM collision table BCKXD1 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2321).

WCLFEW dispatches destroy-vs-create on the NEW status bit (BITB ,X): bit set destroys the cliff, bit clear rebuilds it — so a destroyed cliff returns when a later wave drops its bit (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2304).
IWAVE edge-triggers destruction: EORA WSTATUS,X XORs the old wave's status with the new wave's to find which cliff bits CHANGED (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2022).
IWAVE masks the changed bits to the cliff nibble with ANDA #WBCLS ($F0) before walking WCLFTB — only high-nibble cliff bits drive destruction (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2023).
IWAVE2 reads TBRIDGE, the countdown to the bridge burn, once per inter-wave pass (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1934).

source.verbatim: IWAVE2	LDA	TBRIDGE		TIME TILL BURNS YOUR BRIDGES BEHIND YOU

claim: TBRIDGE is DECremented once per wave setup; seeded at 3, it reaches zero as wave 3 begins (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1936).
When TBRIDGE reaches zero the bridge burns: JSR STBRID starts the bridge-collapsing (flame sweep) routine (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1938).

source.verbatim: JSR	STBRID		START BRIDGE COLAPSING ROUTINE, LEFT TO RT.

claim: BRIDGE is the left half of the bridge solid-fill over the lava (dest $00D3 at the CLIF5 Y-row, width $1B) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1126).
BRIDG2 is the second half of the bridge solid-fill (dest $78D3, width $1E) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1127).
LAVABC (the bridge-burn flame) MODIFIES the CLIF5 landing area column by column as it sweeps (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5258).

source.verbatim: LAVABC	LDX	PDIST,U		MODIFY CLIFF5 LANDING AREA

claim: The burn writes the updated CLIF5 landing bit ($20) back into the RAM landing table LNDXTB — the bridge span loses footing while the island keeps it (JOUSTRV4.SRC:5263).
TRACE (open-questions §4): the "1ST, OR 2ND WAVE?" comment reads TBRIDGE, a countdown, feeding the EMYTIM early-game slowdown — not a wave number (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2202).
TRACE (open-questions §4): the "1ST, 2ND, OR 3RD WAVE?" comment reads TTROLL, a countdown that is nonzero exactly on waves 1-3, feeding the EMYTIM slowdown — not a wave number (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4719).
TRACE (open-questions §5): the CLIF1L cliff record is a 4-word DMA record (collision ptr, source ptr, dest $0145, w/h $1107) (JOUSTI.SRC:54).

TRACE (open-questions §5): CLIF1L's SECOND variant is a 3-word record — same source/dest, height nibble one less ($1106 vs $1107), collision pointer DROPPED — and no game-code path references it (JOUSTI.SRC:55).
TRACE (open-questions §5): the CLIF2 cliff record is a 4-word DMA record (dest $2B51, w/h $2C09) (JOUSTI.SRC:106).
TRACE (open-questions §5): CLIF2's SECOND variant is one scanline shorter ($2C08 vs $2C09) with its collision pointer dropped — the same unconsumed erase-variant shape (JOUSTI.SRC:107).
